speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are here for wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it started after a specific injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis with possible underlying inflammatory arthritis or rheumatoid factor involvement.

I would like to confirm if the pain is localized to the thumb side of the wrist and request an Ultrasound of the right wrist to evaluate the tendons and any inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, Anti-CCP. REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_right_wrist.
